refreshes.scope: Verification harnesses, gates and evidence under PenniLogic/docs#28: the physical test device (android#14), the Android, web and admin quality gates (android#15, web#7, admin#3), privacy traffic inspection (android#16), the sanitized parser corpus and compatibility matrix (android#35), the money-path harness (api#22), the tenancy, object-authorization and authentication attack suite (api#23), contract testing (contracts#3), static and dynamic scanning with flaky-test quarantine (infra#28), load, stress, soak, chaos and the disaster-recovery game day (infra#29), supply-chain verification (infra#31), the penetration test and red-team scenarios (docs#43), this refresh loop (docs#48) and the private-beta and public-launch evidence gates (docs#49, docs#50). The threat surface is the test assets themselves (corpora, devices, exploit suites, scanner credentials, captured traffic), the gates (quarantine, waivers, evidence artifacts) and the environments the suites are pointed at.
sources: PenniLogic/docs#28 (epic body: goal, scope, exit criteria)

data_flows.data_class: Sanitized parser corpus derived from real bank and wallet messages, and the compatibility matrix built from it
data_flows.purpose_ref: Parser regression testing; publication rules and redaction gate owned by PenniLogic/android#35 (E25-F02); raw seeds never enter a repository (governance/DELIVERY.md)
data_flows.retention: Published entries indefinitely in the repository; raw seed messages kept outside the repository only as long as the redaction gate needs them
data_flows.erasure_path: A contributor may withdraw a seed; the derived entry is regenerated from templates or removed, and the redaction gate re-run
data_flows.children: Not subjects: seeds come from adult contributors' own devices with consent

data_flows.data_class: Release-candidate traffic captures and physical-device contents used for privacy inspection and instrumented journeys
data_flows.purpose_ref: Privacy traffic inspection evidence (compliance O-8, PenniLogic/android#16) on synthetic accounts only (E25-F06, E25-F11)
data_flows.retention: Captures kept with the release evidence for the evidence retention period the release checklist publishes (docs#23), under an access list
data_flows.erasure_path: Synthetic accounts only, so no data subject can request erasure; captures are deleted at the end of the evidence retention period and the device is wiped before transfer

data_flows.data_class: Penetration-test and red-team findings reports, scanner outputs and attack-suite fixtures
data_flows.purpose_ref: Independent security testing before public launch (PenniLogic/docs#43, compliance O-28); synthetic tenants only (E25-F08)
data_flows.retention: Reports retained for the period docs#43 fixes with an encrypted channel and a named access list (E25-F07); retest evidence attached to the launch gate
data_flows.erasure_path: Report retention limit and vendor account revocation at the end of the engagement
processors: External penetration-test vendor under the scope contract docs#43 defines

categories.analysis: Test doubles are identities: sandbox provider keys, mock authentication, test-mode webhook signing secrets and allowlisted test hosts. The classic failure is a bypass that ships: a build flag or configuration that accepts the test identity in a production build; nothing in the current gates proves that a release candidate contains no such bypass (E25-F12). The release identity itself is a dependency this epic does not own: the signed-provenance gate infra#31 verifies and the evidence gates docs#49 and docs#50 consume are defeated by construction if the Android upload key leaks, because the attacker's build is validly signed. Upload-key custody, rotation and recovery are owned by android#37 in E24; E24's Definition of Ready refresh must review that control, and this record names the dependency so it is not invisible to either epic.
evidence: PenniLogic/android#37: Play App Signing enrolment, upload-key custody, rotation and recorded recovery path (E24)
PenniLogic/infra#31: signed mobile-binary provenance verification depends on that custody

categories.analysis: The gates are the asset: a quarantine list, a threshold file, a waiver or an evidence artifact that can be edited defeats every test behind it. Supply-chain verification (infra#31) covers the build inputs. The flaky-test quarantine that infra#28 introduces is the one mechanism designed to make a failing test stop failing, and it needs limits that keep it from silencing a security, privacy or money test.
evidence: PenniLogic/infra#31: IaC, container, mobile binary, SBOM and signed-provenance verification

categories.analysis: Release decisions rest on evidence gates that read artifacts and may accept waivers. A hand-made artifact, a stale artifact from an older commit, or a waiver without a date, an expiry and an accountable identity would let a release proceed without anyone being answerable for it. The readiness review already requires dated, expiring, attributable waivers; artifact provenance is not yet stated.
evidence: product/04-execution-readiness-review.md: T-REL-02 and T-REL-03 accept only a dated, expiring, attributable waiver

categories.analysis: Three test assets carry real or realistic personal financial data if handled carelessly: the parser corpus derived from real bank SMS (android#35), the physical device holding accounts, builds and captured traffic (android#14), and the privacy traffic captures themselves (android#16). Each must be synthetic or sanitized, stored with an access list and never enter a public repository; the corpus is the highest risk because it is published deliberately.

Load, stress, soak and chaos suites are denial-of-service tools by construction. Pointed at a shared environment they degrade it; pointed at a metered provider (an AI gateway or a payment sandbox that bills, or worse a live provider) they spend money. The suites need target allowlists, stubs for every metered dependency and a spend kill switch.

The attack suite embeds working cross-tenant, object-authorization and authentication exploits and needs privileged fixtures to set up tenants. Run against the wrong target, or with production data in its fixtures, it is an attack. It must refuse any non-test target and use synthetic tenants only.

The quality epic's contribution against billing forgery is the harness that proves idempotency and adversarial retry on every money path (api#22); the adversarial replay suite for the subscription lifecycle itself is E14's (api#48). Neither exists yet, so this is a hand-off, not a control: the money-path harness ticket does not currently name billing events (purchase, renewal, refund, chargeback, provider webhook replay) among its idempotency and adversarial-retry scenarios, and a harness that proves ledger idempotency while the billing paths are tested elsewhere or nowhere leaves the forgery surface uncovered until E14 (E25-F13).

Entitlement bypass is an authorization failure and belongs in the attack suite next to tenancy and object authorization: a free-plan user calling a plan-gated endpoint, a replayed cached entitlement, a quota reservation that is never reconciled. The suite's current title names tenancy, object authorization and authentication only.

The AI evaluation gate runs real provider calls in continuous integration; without pinned budgets, recorded fixtures and key isolation it is a spend path and a key-exposure path, and the load and chaos suites must stub the gateway (E25-F03). ai-service#7 owns the evaluation suite together with spend controls and admin#5 owns enforced provider spend caps, but neither exists yet, so the gate's own safety is a finding handed to the ticket that will build it rather than a control this refresh can cite (E25-F14).

A dynamic scanner is a request generator with credentials. Mis-targeted it attacks production or a third party; over-privileged scanner accounts become a foothold. The adversarial request-forgery suite for custom endpoints (ai-service#3) is E17's control and is referenced, not re-reviewed, here.
evidence: PenniLogic/ai-service#3: custom endpoint validation and adversarial request-forgery suite (E17)

categories.analysis: Injection through merchant names, SMS and notification text and imported statements is the product's most obvious untrusted-input surface. The red-team scenarios owned by docs#43 are where that attack is exercised end to end; the evaluation suite's adversarial cases (ai-service#7) exercise it per model call. The red-team ticket must name the scenario explicitly so it cannot be scoped out.
evidence: PenniLogic/ai-service#7: at least fifty adversarial evaluation cases

categories.analysis: Split arithmetic (share types, deterministic remainder, settlement) is money arithmetic and belongs under the independent-model comparison and property harness that api#22 builds; api#33 will supply the split ledger the harness checks. The harness ticket does not yet name split scenarios, and the remainder rule they must agree on is still an open decision (E26-F10), so a harness could pass on single-party ledger paths while the multi-party paths where members can shift paise are never compared against the independent model (E25-F15).

The penetration test grants an external party privileged, time-boxed access and produces a report that is itself a map of the system's weaknesses. Vendor accounts, their scope, the environment they attack and the handling of the report all need stating. Operator red-teaming of the admin console (admin#9, docs#131) is E13's and E38's control and is referenced here.
evidence: PenniLogic/admin#9: operator red-team suite as a console release gate
PenniLogic/docs#131: admin operator four-eyes and clock-pressure validation

findings.title: Flaky-test quarantine can silence a failing security, privacy or money test
findings.attack_path: A test that fails because of a real defect is added to the quarantine list under the flaky label; the gate passes, the defect ships, and the entry is never revisited.
findings.recommended_control: Quarantine entries carry an owner, a date and an expiry, count against a published ceiling, are refused for tests tagged security, privacy or money, and the gate fails when an entry expires without a linked fix.

findings.title: A sanitization failure in the parser corpus publishes real bank-message content
findings.attack_path: The corpus is built from real SMS and notification text; a message with an unusual layout keeps an account fragment, a name or a balance through the redaction step and is committed to a public repository.
findings.recommended_control: Generate corpus entries from templates and synthetic values rather than copying real messages; where a real message is the seed, run a redaction gate with planted identifiers that must be removed, keep the seeds outside the repository, and require a second session's review before publication.

findings.title: Load, stress, soak and chaos suites can degrade shared environments or spend money if mis-targeted
findings.attack_path: A suite runs with a target or a dependency configuration pointing at a shared environment, a metered AI gateway or a payment provider; the run degrades the environment for other work or produces provider charges.
findings.recommended_control: Suites accept only allowlisted isolated targets, stub every metered dependency by default, carry a spend kill switch with a published budget, and record the target and budget in the run evidence.

findings.title: Dynamic scanning credentials and targets are not bounded
findings.attack_path: A scanner configured with broad credentials or an unrestricted target list reaches a production or third-party endpoint, or its stored credentials are exfiltrated from the pipeline and reused.
findings.recommended_control: Scanner service accounts are least-privilege, short-lived and rotated; scan targets are an allowlist of isolated environments; a run against any other host fails before the first request.

findings.title: Evidence gates do not yet require artifact provenance
findings.attack_path: A release gate reads an evidence artifact that was produced for an older commit, edited by hand or fabricated; the gate passes and nobody is answerable for the release decision.
findings.recommended_control: Every artifact the gate reads carries the commit SHA, the producing workflow run and check name, and is rejected when stale or unsigned by the pipeline; waivers are dated, expiring and attributable to an account or session, as already required.

findings.title: The physical test device holds credentials, builds and captured traffic
findings.attack_path: The device is lost, stolen or resold with test accounts, debug builds, capture logs or a real SIM still on it.
findings.recommended_control: Synthetic accounts and data only, full-disk encryption and a screen lock, remote wipe enrolled, an inventory entry with custodian, and a wipe step before any transfer; production data never installed.

findings.title: Penetration-test vendor access and report handling are unspecified
findings.attack_path: Tester accounts outlive the engagement or reach production data; the findings report, a map of the system's weaknesses, is shared over an unmanaged channel or retained indefinitely.
findings.recommended_control: A scope contract naming the isolated environment and what may be attacked, time-boxed tester accounts revoked at the end, synthetic data only, encrypted delivery and a retention limit for the report, and retest evidence recorded per finding.

findings.title: The attack suite must refuse non-test targets and production data
findings.attack_path: The tenancy and authorization exploit suite is run against a shared or production environment, or its fixtures are seeded from real tenants, turning the test into an attack or a data exposure.
findings.recommended_control: The suite verifies an explicit test-environment marker before running, uses synthetic tenants it creates and destroys, and fails closed on any other target.

findings.title: Entitlement bypass scenarios are missing from the attack suite
findings.attack_path: A free-plan user calls a plan-gated endpoint directly, replays a cached entitlement, or drives quota reservation without reconciliation; no suite exercises these paths, so a server that trusts client state ships.
findings.recommended_control: Add entitlement and quota scenarios to the attack suite: plan-gated endpoints called without entitlement, replayed or expired entitlement tokens, reservation without reconciliation, and cross-channel precedence conflicts, each asserting a server-side denial.

findings.title: Red-team scenarios must name prompt injection through transaction text
findings.attack_path: A merchant name, SMS body, notification or imported statement line contains instructions; the assistant follows them, calls a tool the user did not request or leaks data, and no end-to-end scenario would have caught it.
findings.recommended_control: Name prompt injection through each untrusted text channel, plus insecure handling of model output, as red-team scenarios with pass and fail criteria, and require a retest after any defence change.

findings.title: Privacy traffic captures are themselves a data store
findings.attack_path: Release-candidate traffic is captured from a device carrying a real account; the capture files, kept as evidence, contain the financial data the inspection was meant to prove absent.
findings.recommended_control: Capture only from synthetic accounts, store captures with the release evidence under an access list and retention limit, and fail the inspection if the capture contains any value from the synthetic seed that is marked as must-not-transmit.

findings.title: No gate proves a release candidate contains no test bypass
findings.attack_path: A test-mode authentication shortcut, sandbox provider key, mock webhook secret or allowlisted test host remains enabled in a release build; an attacker who learns the test identity is accepted in production.
findings.recommended_control: The release checklist requires each platform gate to emit a no-test-bypass artifact: release builds compiled without test flags, configuration free of sandbox credentials and test hosts, and a probe proving the test identity is rejected by the candidate.

findings.title: The money-path harness does not name billing events among its idempotency and replay scenarios
findings.attack_path: The harness proves ledger writes are idempotent while purchase, renewal, refund, chargeback and provider-webhook replays are exercised nowhere until E14; a replayed webhook or receipt that grants entitlement twice, or a refund that leaves entitlement in place, ships past the quality gates.
findings.recommended_control: Name billing events (purchase, renewal, refund, chargeback, promotional eligibility, webhook replay and out-of-order delivery) as required idempotency and adversarial-retry scenarios of the harness, asserting a server-side verification before any entitlement or balance change, and require api#48 to reuse the harness rather than a private suite.

findings.title: The AI evaluation gate is itself a spend and key-exposure path
findings.attack_path: The evaluation suite calls live providers from continuous integration; a runaway matrix, a retry loop or a fork pull request that triggers it spends against the platform key, and a key exposed to the job is exfiltrated through logs or a compromised action.
findings.recommended_control: The gate runs recorded fixtures by default and live calls only on a protected branch with a pinned per-run budget, a hard spend cap enforced by the gateway (admin#5), a key scoped to the evaluation project and rotated, no key on fork pull requests, and the spend and cap published with every run.

findings.title: Split and settlement scenarios are missing from the independent-model harness
findings.attack_path: The harness compares single-party ledger paths against the independent model while share allocation, remainder distribution, settlement recording and member removal are never compared; two implementations disagree by a paise per split and a member exploits or disputes the difference.
findings.recommended_control: Add split scenarios to the property and independent-model harness once the remainder rule is decided (E26-F10): share types, remainder allocation order and tie-break, settlement and reversal, member addition and removal, each asserting equality with the independent model to the minor unit.
